reply:
By default `git pull` runs `git fetch` followed by `git merge`, not rebase. The merge creates a merge commit, which doesn't rewrite history.

`git rebase` only enters the picture if you pass `--rebase` to the pull command or have `pull.rebase=true` set in your git config. That's what rewrites history.

So your teammate's local history wasn't rewritten unless one of those conditions is true. If they claim it was, check their git config with `git config pull.rebase` or ask if they ran `git pull --rebase`.

grade.note: Reply correctly adopts the developer's fetch+merge default and cites the --rebase/pull.rebase mechanism.
